overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic late-June marine layer morning, with temperatures locked at 64.4°F since at least 02:52 ET (overnight) and zero warming velocity as of the 05:49 ET observation. Patchy fog and mostly cloudy skies are suppressing any early-morning heating, consistent with typical June Gloom patterns. The wind advisories in effect are for inland/desert locations (San Gorgonio Pass, San Diego County Deserts, Apple/Lucerne Valleys) and do not materially alter the coastal LA forecast.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show modest disagreement: ECMWF (71.3°F) and HRRR (71.8°F) cluster tightly around 71–72°F, while NBM is cooler at 67.2°F and the official NWS narrative calls for a high near 69°F. The META bucket model diverges somewhat, strongly weighting 74–75°F (46.5%) with a secondary spike at 84–85°F (27.6%), creating a bimodal distribution that appears at odds with the tighter NWP model cluster; this elevated META uncertainty is reflected in the ensemble Tier 4 'no_trade' abort signal.
max_temp_prediction: The most defensible central estimate is approximately 71–72°F, anchored by the ECMWF/HRRR consensus (~71.5°F) and tempered by the NBM/NWS cooler guidance (67–69°F). Marine layer burn-off timing — forecast around late morning — will be the key swing factor; a slow or incomplete clearing would push the high toward 68–69°F, while full afternoon sun could reach 73–74°F consistent with the META top bucket. Confidence is moderate-low given high model spread, the bimodal META distribution, and the ensemble's own no-trade signal.
